events.region: San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Santa Cruz Mountains; Northern Monterey Bay
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 1228 PM PST, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 8
miles southwest of Boulder Creek, or 11 miles northwest of Santa
Cruz, moving southeast at 35 mph.

HAZARD...Landspouts, wind gusts up to 40 mph, and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Minor damage to outdoor objects is possible. Gusty winds
could knock down tree limbs and blow around unsecured
objects.

Locations impacted include...
Santa Cruz, Scotts Valley, Capitola, Live Oak, Felton, Twin Lakes,
Opal Cliffs, Soquel, Aptos and Rio Del Mar.

events.region: Inland Palm Beach County; Metro Palm Beach County; Inland Broward County; Metro Broward County; Inland Miami-Dade County; Metropolitan Miami Dade; Coastal Palm Beach County; Coastal Broward County; Coastal Miami Dade County; Far South Miami-Dade County
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal
Palm Beach County, Far South Miami-Dade County, Inland Broward
County, Inland Miami-Dade County, Inland Palm Beach County, Metro
Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County and Metropolitan Miami
Dade.

* WHEN...Through Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Widespread 3 to 5 inches of rain have fallen across the east
coast of South Florida over the past several days, with pockets
of 8 to 15 inches. Areas having received these higher end amounts
are most susceptible to today's forecast rain amounts. Common
rainfall amounts in locations impacted by showers for the rest of
the afternoon and into tonight will be 1 to 2 inches, with the
isolated high end amounts closer to 3 to 5 inches.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: San Francisco
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.4 ft of
inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves of 18 to 24 ft with up to 30 ft at favored
break points.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 11 AM PST
Saturday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45 AM
Friday and 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 8:15 AM
Saturday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively. The
Pacific Coast will likely be added to the Advisory as early as
Sunday with the San Francisco and San Pablo Bays upgraded to a
Coastal Flood Warning as we approach "King Tides".
